newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cookson skirts year low after results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cookson skirts year low after results.

text.p: Shares in the Cookson Group came close to hitting a new year low on Thursday after it reported six-month results which warned of a 25 million pounds second-half charge and ignited concern over debt and cash flow.

Pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits for the six months ended June 30 were 85.3 million pounds ($133.8 million), up five percent against a backdrop of difficult market conditions which plagued two-thirds of the business.
Analysts said they saw further profit downgrades ahead, leading to Cookson shares sliding 10 pence to 247. The share price was just above the 1996 low of 244.5 pence at 1130 GMT.
"It has been a challenging six months, in which the majority of our businesses experienced difficult trading conditions," chairman Bob Malpas said in the results statement.
Despite weak markets, group sales rose six percent to 933 million pounds. The dividend was up 11 percent at 3.9 pence.
Restructuring within the group continued, resulting in the warning of a 25 million charge in the second-half results.
The charge relates to further streamlining which will be implemented over the next few months. The payback is foreseen within two to three years, Cookson said.
But the results met with a sour reaction from the market.
Traders said investors were disappointed at Cookson's capital outflow and debt figures and news of the charge ahead.
"These are not spectacular figures and we think we're going to see a lot of downgrades," one dealer said.
One analyst at a leading London investment house said he was considering downgrading Cookson from "hold" but said no decision had yet been taken.
Cookson has already had a rocky ride on the share market this year.
It faced a series of full-year profit downgrades through the summer, pushing the shares to their current lows, which led to Cookson being ousted from the premier FTSE 100 share index.
Among the reasons for the earlier downgrades was concern about weakness in its Electronic Materials division, which has now been borne out.

Looking at a divisional breakdown of the results, Advanced Refractories, Cookson Matthey Ceramics, Engineered Products and Plastics all achieved better profits and margins. But Electronic Materials saw a four percent fall in profits. ($1=.6373 Pound)
